content.content:
Apply these criteria to the dependent's recorded decision node, reading it against rptlovpt, then qwzwpxws; nothing runs, and no behaviour is probed.

(1) Subject. A decision whose content is still a placeholder or otherwise records no commitment leaves the check with no subject to read; that absence is a finding, named as such.

(2) The thing whose presentation is changed (rptlovpt). The entry the dependent presents is the Content section's path entry as that decision records it — the control whose activation the decision states — and the dependent's commitment is presentation over that entry, not a re-decision of it. Fail on any element that turns the entry into inert content or into a presentation whose activation the decision does not state, one that gives the entry a second activation or a differing outcome, one that attaches the presentation to something other than that entry, or one that states a rule only that decision states: an outcome, an activation input or variant, a transport, message or command, a file or path resolution or normalization rule, or behaviour for a path that names no file. If that decision carries no recorded commitment about such an entry, the use has nothing to be read against, and that absence is a finding.

(3) The value the entry is part of (qwzwpxws). Where content.ref is a list of paths, that decision presents the content type together with those repo-relative paths in the same monospaced block, with the section's label, its place in the fixed kind, content, rationale order and the other sections unchanged. Fail on any element of the dependent that withholds, replaces or reorders those paths, reintroduces a body the node does not carry, moves the paths out of that block, duplicates them in a second surface or presents them outside that section, or varies that presentation by content.type beyond what that decision states, naming it.

(4) Non-contradiction. No element of the dependent contradicts rptlovpt or qwzwpxws. Fail on any contradicting element, naming it and the prerequisite involved.

(5) Decidability. From the recorded statement alone a reviewer must be able to name an observation that would refute it without supplying a rule the dependent does not state — an observation about the entry, about the paths presented with it, or about that entry's activation in the panel. If no such observation can be named from the statement, that is a finding.
content.rationale:
Both prerequisites are inline prose commitments — rptlovpt is a design decision about what a ref-path entry is and what activating it does, qwzwpxws about how the Content section renders a type together with a path list — and the dependent is inline prose about how such an entry is presented, so this edge is the evaluation matrix's natural-to-natural cell and takes the gate form: a reviewer reads the recorded decision against the recorded prerequisites and checks non-violation, and nothing runs. A runnable check would have to probe the rendering of a prose child, which the strictness rule denies, and it would have to invent the rendering observable the dependent is free to state differently; that belongs to a decision whose child is code, not to this edge.

Non-violation on the surface alone would leave the one way this decision can go wrong ungated. An appearance commitment is easy to state as presentation and mean more: presenting the paths somewhere other than the monospaced block, replacing them with whatever the presentation's own label happens to say, reintroducing a body the node does not carry because the entry now looks like something that carries one, or sliding an activation, an opening rule or a path-resolution rule in behind the presentation while contradicting neither prerequisite in so many words. The criteria therefore keep the two uses apart rather than checking the prose: against rptlovpt, the entry being presented is the control that decision records, and nothing about what it is or what activating it does is re-decided; against qwzwpxws, the paths, their block and the section's frame are untouched by the presentation. Clause (5) keeps the commitment decidable at review time: a statement of presentation from which no refuting observation can be named has settled nothing a reviewer can check.

Every clause is decidable by reading two or three recorded nodes, names no endpoint-specific element in advance — which element fails is the check's output, never the criterion — demands no wording of the dependent, and states no rule its prerequisites do not, so it survives the dependent being rewritten without changing what it decides.
